rationale: C11 is a direct predecessor letter for the same office and supplies nearly the entire operative structure of the child: designation as Supreme Allied Commander, Atlantic; reference to NATO Standing Group terms governing responsibilities and authority; assignment of operational command over U.S. Atlantic forces to the extent necessary for the mission; authority to use military and civilian staff in appropriate numbers and grades; and transmission of copies to the Secretaries of State and Defense for guidance. C14 is an earlier closely parallel Supreme Allied Commander letter, but C11 matches the specific Atlantic command and language much more closely. C13 has only a weaker staffing-authority parallel.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Your responsibilities and authority as the Supreme Allied Commander, Atlantic, are contained in the Terms of Reference issued by the Standing Group of the Military Committee of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am informed that the Standing Group of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization will issue a directive to you concerning your responsibilities and authority as the Supreme Allied Commander, Atlantic.
shared_material.explanation: Both place the commander's responsibilities and authority in an instrument issued by NATO's Standing Group.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The United States Armed Forces assigned to the United States Atlantic Command will continue to remain under your operational command to the extent necessary for the accomplishment of your mission.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: You are hereby assigned operational command, of the United States Armed forces assigned to the U.S. Atlantic Command, to the extent necessary for the accomplishment of your mission.
shared_material.explanation: This is substantially the same operative command provision, adjusted to reflect continuity in office.

shared_material.child_excerpt: You are hereby authorized to use officers and enlisted personnel of the United States Armed Forces and civilian employees of the United States Government on your staff as you consider appropriate in numbers and grades as necessary.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: You are hereby authorized to use officers and enlisted personnel of the U.S. Armed forces and civilian employees of the U.S. Government, on your staff as you consider appropriate in numbers and grades as necessary.
shared_material.explanation: The staffing authorization is nearly verbatim.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am sending copies of this letter to the Secretary of State and to the Secretary of Defense for their guidance.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am sending copies of this letter to the Secretary of State and to the Secretary of Defense for their guidance.
shared_material.explanation: The closing administrative sentence is identical and reinforces the broader sequence-level match.
